summary: Aermotor MC-39 fire tower in Bedford County, Virginia, with radio gear added; NHLR-registered 2026; listed as administered by Appalachian Power. Build date, staffing and access unknown.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 tower, 59 feet 4 inches from the ground to the floor of the cab; bottom two flights of stairs removed and radio equipment mounted, adding about 15 to 20 feet

access.note: No source read says whether the public may climb the tower; Appalachian Power is listed as administrator.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, registered in 2026, names Appalachian Power as administrator. The Forest Lookouts page heading names the Virginia Department of Forestry, with no dates. The story reports both and treats the NHLR listing as current.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. NHLR is the only detailed source; Forest Lookouts gives only a county and an agency heading, and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list confirms the tower is standing. No construction date appears in any source read. The brief record elevation (456.6 m) matches NHLR's 1,498 ft. A Lake News article on Smith Mountain fire tower history (lakemagazine.life) turned up in search but the site returned HTTP 429 on two tries, so it was not read or cited. A Facebook group post and a YouTube video also describe the tower but could not be read. Do not confuse with the Alabama Smith Mountain lookout (us-al-smith-mountain) or the separate Bedford lookout in Virginia (us-va-bedford). The agency conflict is not resolved by any source. Not verified: whether the radio equipment is still mounted, and who now has access. No new photos.
